messages.subject: Convergence diagnostics
parts:
I have just started learning to use 'nimble'. It looks like a very useful addition to the current softwares on hierarchical models and MCMC. Thanks for developing this. Now to my questions (naive, almost certainly): 

1) How do I run several chains to see if I have convergence and mixing? I can write a do loop, I guess. But is there a simple option such as n.chains in JAGS? Is there a simple way to get different diagnostics or do I have to feed the output to CODA to get it? 

2) If I have new data set, do I have to recompile the model with the new data? 

Thanks, Perry and colleagues, for your wonderful work.

Subhash

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Convergence diagnostics
parts:
Hi Subhash,

Nice to see you here and thanks for the message.

1. No, it is of course a minor point but we have not automated the running of multiple chains.  Yes, feeding the output to CODA makes sense.  In MCMCsuite (and compareMCMC, a higher level version in upcoming 0.5 release soon) we use coda::effectiveSize to estimate the effective sample size, but we don’t otherwise access coda tools automatically.

2. No, you can just assign the data to the appropriate variables in the model.

For example

myCode <- nimbleCode({ ## world’s simplest model
  mu ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  y ~ dnorm(mu, 1)
})

myModel <- nimbleModel(myCode, data = list(y = 1.23))

CmyModel <- compileNimble(myModel)
CmyModel$y  ## should be 1.23, the value you happened to set at model definition
CmyModel$y <- 2.34 ## now it has a new value
## if you want to simulate data, you must provide includeData = TRUE to the simulate function
## otherwise it will respect data labels and not overwrite values in those nodes
CmyModel$mu <- 0.5 ## need a value here for simulation of y to produce something meaningful
simulate(CmyModel, ‘y’, includeData = TRUE)
calculate(CmyModel) ## update logProbs if needed

Best
Perry
